bug_semantics: IndexFile.from_tree appends caller-controlled treeish values after its own --index-output=<temporary-index> argument and invokes git read-tree without an unsafe-option guard or option/operand separator; reset delegates its caller-controlled commit to from_tree, while merge_tree appends caller-controlled base and rhs values to another unguarded read-tree invocation. Supplying --index-output=<attacker-chosen-writable-path> is therefore parsed as an option, and Git's last-occurrence-wins behavior overrides from_tree's temporary path, replacing the chosen file with a valid DIRC git-index blob. The attacker controls the destination, not arbitrary replacement bytes, yielding destructive arbitrary file overwrite rather than code execution.
flaw_origin: babf5765da3e328cc1060cb9b37fbdeb6fd58350 is the original implementation of Index.from_tree, not a move or refactor: it created arg_list, appended GitPython's own --index-output temporary path, extended the same argv with unvalidated *treeish, and called repo.git.read_tree(*arg_list, **kwargs). Its direct parent has no from_tree or read_tree sink. f6c8072daa942e9850b9d7a78bd2a9851c48cd2c later added the independently vulnerable merge_tree base/rhs forwarding, 58fb1187b7b8f1e62d3930bdba9be5aba47a52c6 later made reset delegate to from_tree, and af32b6e0ad4ab244dc70a5ade0f8a27ab45942f8 merely moved the extant implementation into the index package; none supersedes the earliest true BIC.
ai_marker: Absent on BIC babf5765da3e328cc1060cb9b37fbdeb6fd58350. `git cat-file -p` shows human author and committer Sebastian Thiel <byronimo@gmail.com>, the one-line subject 'Initial version of merge including tests for one-way, two-way and tree-way merge', and no Co-authored-by, Assisted-by, Generated-with, agent, bot, or other AI marker/trailer.
evidence: First-party GHSA-4gmw-gg2m-w46p (referenced by the assigned GHSA-7jx3-jqcp-hhgc bundle) documents the three entrypoints, argv shape, --index-output last-wins overwrite, DIRC output, affected <=3.1.57 and patched >=3.1.58. In the validated clone, `git log --all --reverse -S'read_tree' -- '*.py'` identifies babf5765da3e328cc1060cb9b37fbdeb6fd58350 as the earliest read_tree addition; `git log --all --reverse -S'arg_list.extend(treeish)' -- '*.py'` independently identifies the same commit, and `git log 96a888f4d782cb2f80452148e48e60ce4af6d541 -L 331,392:git/index/base.py` traces current from_tree lineage back to that original lib/git/index.py implementation. `git show babf5765da3e328cc1060cb9b37fbdeb6fd58350 -- '*.py'` shows arg_list.append('--index-output=%s' % tmp_index), arg_list.extend(treeish), then repo.git.read_tree(*arg_list, **kwargs). Direct parent verification with `git grep -n -e 'def from_tree' -e 'read_tree' -e 'arg_list.extend(treeish)' b9d6494f1075e5370a20e406c3edb102fca12854 -- lib/git/index.py` returns no matches. `git show f6c8072daa942e9850b9d7a78bd2a9851c48cd2c` shows merge_tree appending base/rhs and invoking self.repo.git.read_tree(args); `git show 58fb1187b7b8f1e62d3930bdba9be5aba47a52c6` shows reset's new `type(self).from_tree(self.repo, commit)` delegation. `git show 9b5dcaf85da5946dbf69dcd53f9edba08f760b32` shows the direct fix adding unsafe_git_read_tree_options=['--index-output'], check_unsafe_options over both positional and keyword candidates, and allow_unsafe_options plumbing to from_tree, merge_tree, and reset. `git grep` at tag 3.1.57 finds the two unguarded read_tree sinks and no unsafe_git_read_tree_options; at 3.1.58 it finds both new guards. `git tag --contains 9b5dcaf85da5946dbf69dcd53f9edba08f760b32 --sort=version:refname` returns only 3.1.58 and 3.1.59. `git tag --contains babf5765da3e328cc1060cb9b37fbdeb6fd58350 --sort=version:refname` starts at 0.2.0-beta1 and continues through 3.1.57, establishing the source-level introduction boundary more precisely than the advisory's open-ended <=3.1.57 range. Finally, `git cat-file -p babf5765da3e328cc1060cb9b37fbdeb6fd58350` supplies the exact parent and proves the BIC commit-object marker absence.
reasoning: The vulnerability existed as soon as the original from_tree implementation put caller-controlled strings into an option-parsing position of git read-tree, so babf5765da3e328cc1060cb9b37fbdeb6fd58350 is the smallest causal BIC. The later merge_tree and reset commits broadened the reachable API surface but did not originate the already exploitable mechanism, and the package split was only a move. The direct parent lacks both the API and sink. Commit 9b5dcaf85da5946dbf69dcd53f9edba08f760b32 closes every documented entrypoint and is first released in 3.1.58. Although the 2026 fix commit itself contains GPT 5.6 assistance/co-author trailers, the protocol judges only the 2009 BIC commit object; that object is human-authored and has no AI signal, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
